column15: Nikka's original 1934 Hokkaido distillery, coal-fired direct-flame stills; traditionally the peatier/smokier half of Nikka's pair (vs Miyagikyo). Wikipedia's own distillery article is a peat-silent stub; the only citation reachable this session is a Nonjatta blog search hit titled "Yoichi 12 - fruit and peat" -- real but weak evidence. Official Nikka pages, distiller.com, dekanta.com and whisky.com/whiskybase were all blocked (403/404/cert errors) this session. Set medium rather than heavy since Yoichi is generally described as less extreme than Islay's heaviest malts, but a human should re-verify against a stronger source. One of this batch's highest-value rows per the brief.

Nikka's second (1969) distillery near Sendai, built deliberately as a lighter/fruitier counterpart to Yoichi (steam-heated stills vs Yoichi's coal-fired ones). Whisky-writer consensus is unpeated/very light, but no source stating this explicitly was reachable this session (official Nikka pages 403, distiller.com 404, dekanta.com 404, nonjatta index pages carried no body text) -- left unknown rather than asserted from recall alone.

Orkney distillery. Wikipedia (fetched this session): "Highland Park uses the local peat, which contains a higher proportion of heather than many other peats" -- moderate, heather-inflected smoke rather than Islay-heavy. Same facts as existing rows in batches 13/16; slug reused.

Wikipedia's La Martiniquaise article lists "Sir Edward's" under its Blended Scotch whisky brands, alongside Cutty Sark and Label 5, confirming French ownership -- this project's own be/CLAUDE.md independently records "Bardinet" as the legal producer read off a real winebutik detail page, and the same Wikipedia article's later acquisitions are captioned "La Martiniquaise-Bardinet", so the two sources agree it is one group. No citation found for the base range's own peat level, left unknown. This batch's own sample "Sir Edwards Smoky" is the brief's own worked example of a distinctly smoky/peated expression of the SAME producer -- captured as a rule below rather than a second producer row, per the brief's explicit instruction.

Legal producer "Glen Turner" per this project's own be/CLAUDE.md, read directly off a real alcomag/winebutik detail page's "Виробник" field (first-party scrape evidence, not a URL fetched this session, hence no sourceUrls here). This batch's only sample, "Glen Clan Smoky Peated Blend", names its own peat character directly in the product name -- captured as a rule below; base/default peatProfile left unknown since no non-smoky expression is evidenced.

La Martiniquaise's own Wikipedia brand list piped-links "Glen Turner" to the Glen Moray distillery article ([[Glen Moray distillery|Glen Turner]]) -- i.e. Glen Moray's malt sold under a second brand name; there is no independent "Glen Turner" whisky article (that title belongs to a rugby league player). parentSlug=glen-moray, a real distillery already present with its own citations in batches 05/12/16 of this project, not re-emitted here. Same slug and facts as batch 12's existing row for consistency.
Own-label blended Scotch, 4 products in this batch. No web presence found this session (Wikipedia search returned nothing on point); country/type per the catalogue's own guess.
Own-label blended Scotch, 3 products in this batch. No web presence found this session.
Own-label blended Scotch (not the bank), 2 products in this batch. No web presence found this session.
Mallows suggests a marshmallow-flavoured novelty bourbon liqueur rather than a straight whiskey. Producer not identified this session; searches returned nothing on point.

Historic Irish whiskey name (Samuel Gelston's, est. 1808); confirmed as a live current brand by its sponsorship of Northern Ireland's Irish Cup football competition ("Samuel Gelston's Whiskey Irish Cup") on Wikipedia. Owner is taken from this batch's own sample "Gelston's Halewood" (direct catalogue evidence; Halewood's own site/pages were unreachable this session -ECONNREFUSED). defaultTypeName left empty: historically a blend, but catalogue guesses single malt for both samples and the current Halewood-era range was not confirmed either way.
Historic-sounding Scotch blend name; no citation found this session (Wikipedia search returned nothing on point).

No country stated by the catalogue and no producer identified this session. defaultTypeName=rye taken from the catalogue's own guess; peatProfile=none rests on the general rye-whiskey-is-unpeated category convention (peated malt is not used in American rye mashbills), not a brand-specific source.
No web presence found this session.
Own-label blend ("Special Reserve"), no web presence found this session.

Contrary to my first guess (a New Zealand independent bottler), 36southwhisky.com redirects straight to morrisofrutherglen.com/pages/36-south-whisky: 36 South is produced by Morris of Rutherglen in Victoria, Australia (name references 36 degrees south latitude), matching the catalogue's own AU guess. "36 South Double Grain Whisky" made from local wheat/barley; page's own tasting language ("smooth yet complex") has no smoke/peat descriptor -- no cask-finish/Morris-cask connection stated on that page despite the sample name.

Confirmed by this project's own reference authority table (region=Lowland, owner=Morrison Scotch Whisky Distillers, malt, operating) -- matches the catalogue's own sample naming "Aberargie Morrison" directly. Official site (fetched this session) states only "balanced, elegant" character and first-fill bourbon/sherry cask maturation, with no explicit peat/unpeated statement, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than guessed.

No web presence found this session (official domain unreachable, Wikipedia search returned nothing but Simpsons/Ireland false positives). Alias kept at any-scope only after judgement that "Bart's" (6 chars incl. apostrophe) is a reasonably distinctive token for a whisky catalogue -- flag for reviewer if this proves too permissive.

Possibly named for the Beara Peninsula, Co. Cork; no producer/distillery identified this session (official domain unreachable). defaultTypeName left empty: catalogue types the bare "Beara" sample as grain but its "Black Cask Blend" sibling as blend.
No web presence found this session. The "Butterscotch Liquor" sample suggests a flavoured whiskey liqueur variant rather than a straight whiskey for that specific expression.

Catalogue lists this same name 3 times with inconsistent country/type (DE/blend, US/rye, US/blend); countryCode=US taken as the majority value, not a confirmed fact. No producer identified this session.

No producer identified this session (no useful search hits). peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category convention, not a brand-specific source (matches this project's own batch-08 precedent for an equally unconfirmed US bourbon label).

Blairfindy is a real historic place/castle name in the Glenlivet area of Speyside (Wikipedia's Glenlivet article surfaces it), likely used here as an independent single-cask label name rather than a distillery of its own -- region/legalRegion given from that toponymy alone (low confidence). Treated as an undisclosed-origin label per the brief's rule 3: producer and true source distillery not guessed.

Single generic colour-word name; could not be identified as any specific brand and is below the 5-character alias floor regardless. Kept as a minimal row only so the (necessarily brand-scope) alias exists; note in alias.tsv that it will not resolve in-name.

Official site (fetched this session): "The most awarded single malt whisky distillery in America", Blue Ridge Mountains, Virginia. No peat/smoke mention anywhere on the fetched page; American single malt without a stated peated line, so peatProfile=none rests on that absence plus general category convention rather than an explicit "unpeated" statement. "Courage & Conviction" is confirmed on the same page as a distinct in-house brand -- see that row (parentSlug points here).

Virginia Distillery Company's flagship 100%-Virginia-distilled single malt line, cask-finished (Bourbon/Sherry/Cuvee/etc.) -- named explicitly on the official site as "our Courage & Conviction brand". No peat/smoke stated; peatProfile=none by the same reasoning as the parent row.
Likely named after the Irish folk-song character "Bold Thady Quill"; no producer identified this session.

Bouteille is simply French for "bottle" -- this may be a scraping/page-structure artifact (a label word mistaken for the brand) rather than a genuine brand name; flagged for human review rather than skipped outright, since it is plausibly real French whisky with an unidentifiable brand string. No producer found this session either way.

Peat level is genuinely vintage-dependent, not a fixed house style: Wikipedia -- "Between May 1969 and July 1973, Brora produced a heavily peated whisky... Most of the whisky produced as Brora after 1973 is in the lightly peated Highland style." scotchwhisky.com adds nuance: peating dropped after 1977 but "occasional heavily smoky expressions from the 1980s" still exist, so bottlings vary from "immensely oily and smoky" to "the merest exhalation of peat" depending on cask/vintage. This batch's sample, "Brora 2010 9th Release" (a Diageo Special Release), could be either without knowing its distillation vintage, so peatProfile is left unknown rather than defaulted to one band -- this is the safe, correct answer for this specific distillery, not a research gap.

Diageo's largest grain distillery (est. by John Haig, 1824); produces Cameron Brig and Haig Club single grain whiskies (confirmed via scotchwhisky.com, fetched this session). Region/legalRegion deliberately left empty: this project's own reference authority table (wikipedia-scotland-distilleries.tsv) lists Cameronbridge's region as blank despite its Fife/Lowland geography, and the brief states that table wins on disagreement -- not asserting Lowland here even though batch 04's existing row does. Grain whisky is not peated by standard convention; no source states it explicitly for this distillery, but no grain distillery of this kind is known to use peated malt.

Collingwood, Ontario; triple-distilled continuous still, aged in charred white oak. Introduced 1967 by Brown-Forman, sold to Sazerac Company in 2020 together with Early Times (same reference confirms both sales in one transaction). Canadian whisky does not use peated malt by convention; no explicit statement found, category-level inference.

Independent bottling range of Ian Macleod Distillers Ltd (Broxburn; family-owned since 1933; also owns Glengoyne/Tamdhu/Rosebank distilleries and the peated Smokehead brand) -- confirmed parent company via Wikipedia. "Chieftain's" itself is not named on that page but is directly evidenced by this batch's own sample, "Chieftain's The Cigar Malt (Ian Macleod)", which states the parent in the product name itself. "The Cigar Malt" names no source distillery, so it is left unresolved (undisclosed-cask label) rather than guessed. Bottler has no single house peat level.
No country stated by the catalogue; own-label, no web presence found this session.

No country stated by the catalogue and no specific producer identified this session (named for the Kentucky waterfall). peatProfile=none rests on the general bourbon-is-unpeated category convention, not a brand-specific source.

The Dubliner Irish Whiskey is a real retail brand but its current owner could not be confirmed this session (thedublinerwhiskey.com does not resolve, no Wikipedia article). "Bourbon Cask" is a cask-finish descriptor, not evidence of American whiskey.

Producer not identified this session (guessed Echlinville Distillery and ruled it out -- its own site lists no "Element" brand). IMPORTANT: this project's own be/CLAUDE.md documents that the catalogue separately holds "Elements of Islay", "M&H Elements" and "Glenmorangie Elementa" as unrelated products specifically as an example of why the 5-character alias floor exists -- so the alias is deliberately kept at brand scope only; it will not resolve either "Element Fusion" or "Element Lore" in-name, which is the correct, honest outcome here.

Northern California craft whiskey producer. Official site (fetched this session) confirms "Emerald Giant" as a rye whiskey; range also spans bourbon and a "Foggy Burl Single Malt", so defaultTypeName is left empty. No peat/smoke mentioned anywhere on the fetched page; rye/bourbon mashbills do not use peated malt by convention.

Made by Spirit of Yorkshire Distillery Ltd, Hunmanby (founded 2016, first release 2019, per Wikipedia's list of English distilleries). Official site's own tasting notes for four expressions (Flagship, Moscatel Sherry Cask, STR Red Wine Cask, Yorkshire Day 2026) list only honey/vanilla/citrus/caramel/biscuit/fruit-cake descriptors with zero smoke/peat language across all of them -- inferred none from that consistent absence rather than an explicit "unpeated" statement.

Primarily a jenever/gin distillery (Bachte-Maria-Leerne, since 1880) that also bottles whisky. Official site (fetched this session) confirms a "Single Malt Whisky" described as "100% aged in Sherry casks" -- matches this batch's own "Fillers Sherry Cask(/Strength)" samples exactly (note the catalogue's own spelling drops one 'l'). No peat mentioned on either source.

Producer not identified this session; "Irish Honey" suggests a honey-flavoured whiskey liqueur akin to Irish Mist/Bushmills Irish Honey. Alias kept at brand scope only: "Finity" is a substring of the unrelated common word/brand "Infinity", a real collision risk for in-name matching.

Grimsby, Ontario; launched 1992 by John Hall (Kittling Ridge), bought by Campari Group in 2014. Blended Canadian whisky (rye/barley/corn distilled and aged separately, blended). No peat mentioned; Canadian whisky convention is unpeated.

Could not identify the producer this session -- no Wikipedia article, no useful search hits (tried Ben Nevis Distillery as a plausible geographic link since Glencoe is near Fort William/Ben Nevis; that distillery's own Wikipedia article does not mention a "Glencoe" brand, so not asserted). Treated as an undisclosed-origin single malt label per the brief's rule 3 -- kind=blend used only as the closest available bucket, not because it is actually a blended-type whisky.

World's best-known unpeated Speyside malt; the Wikipedia article does not discuss peat explicitly (it is simply not a live question for this distillery), so peatProfile=none rests on this being one of the most extensively documented unpeated house styles in Scotch whisky, not a single quoted sentence.

Tallest stills in Scotland; unpeated house style. The article does not explicitly say "unpeated" (fetched and checked this session) but the entire range described has no smoke/peat character, and Glenmorangie's one-off peated bottling (Finealta) is itself always marketed as the exception precisely because the core range never is.

Genuinely complicated, and this session's research changes the picture other batches used: Wikipedia (fetched here) says malt is traditionally "dried in a kiln over peat smoke" as part of the GENERAL process description (not only a special edition), the current range explicitly includes "7 Years Old Peat Smoked" and "10 Years Old Peat Smoked" alongside unpeated-sounding lines (Triple Wood, 12/15 Years Old), and a November 2024 announcement states Glenturret "will remove peat from production starting 2025" (i.e. peat was in standard use up to that point, not just in a rare special bottling). This directly complicates batch 13's confident peatProfile=none for this same slug -- flagging for reviewer reconciliation. peatProfile is left unknown here rather than guessing a bandwidth for a moving target; the explicitly named "Peat Smoked"/"Peated" expressions are captured via the rule below instead (matches this batch's own sample "Glenturret Peated" and existing precedent in batch 07's rule.tsv).

Catalogue types this IE-country product as "bourbon", which is definitionally impossible for a genuine Irish whiskey -- likely a mislabeled type on a small Irish whiskey brand rather than an actual bourbon. Producer not identified this session.

Consistently typed "malt" across this batch's 5 samples (cask-finish variants: cider/porto/sherry/original), suggesting a small Spanish blended/vatted-malt whisky brand. Producer not confirmed this session: haranwhisky.com does not resolve, and haran.es redirects to an unrelated Basque geology/topography firm (haran.eus) with no whisky connection. kind=blend used as the closest bucket for an unconfirmed producer, per this project's undisclosed-origin convention.

Kentucky bourbon brand sold by Brown-Forman to Sazerac in 2020 alongside Canadian Mist; the cited page confirms that sale. Bourbon does not use peated malt. Row added during the P1.7 cross-check: agent 17 emitted the alias but no producer, which the merge reported as a dangling reference.
